questions.question_text: Rectangles A and B both have perimeter $34\text{ cm}$. A has length $10\text{ cm}$ and B has length $13\text{ cm}$. Find the missing widths and areas. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A has area $70\text{ cm}^2$ and B has area $52\text{ cm}^2$.
A has area $240\text{ cm}^2$ and B has area $273\text{ cm}^2$.
options.why: Subtracted each length from the full perimeter rather than half: $10\times(34-10)=240$ and $13\times(34-13)=273$.

Used the common perimeter as the area, assuming that equal perimeters give equal areas.

questions.solution_text:
**Find or list the rectangle dimensions and check the area.**
The length and width add to $34\div2=17\text{ cm}$.
A's width is $17-10=7\text{ cm}$.
B's width is $17-13=4\text{ cm}$.

**Calculate the required areas or perimeters.**
$A_A=10\times7=70\text{ cm}^2$.
$A_B=13\times4=52\text{ cm}^2$.

**Compare the results or check the required condition.**
A has area $70\text{ cm}^2$ and B has area $52\text{ cm}^2$, despite their equal perimeters.
